Egyptian Hospitality Industry Feels Impact as Foreign Sanctions Hit Major Hotels

Cairo – The Egyptian hospitality sector is facing mounting challenges as a new round of international sanctions, announced last week, targets hotel operators with alleged ties to disputed regional activities. The sanctions, imposed by a coalition of Western nations, have led to the freezing of assets and temporary blockades at several prominent hotels, including the Nile Oasis and Red Sea Sun Resort chains.

Industry representatives say the measures have caused significant disruptions, with more than a dozen properties in Cairo, Alexandria, and Hurghada unable to process international bookings or access overseas accounts. “We have hundreds of rooms sitting empty and staff unsure about their future,” said Sameh El-Sayed, general manager at Nile Oasis Downtown. “Our revenues have dropped by 60% in just a few days.”

The Egyptian Association of Hospitality Enterprises reported that over 3,000 hospitality workers have been placed on unpaid leave since the sanctions came into effect. “Many of our members are struggling to meet payroll and keep essential services running,” explained association spokesperson Amira Hassan. “We are urgently seeking guidance from authorities and hope the situation will be resolved soon.”

Hotel workers held a demonstration outside the Ministry of Tourism on Monday, calling for government intervention to safeguard jobs and ensure the sector’s stability. “We rely on this work to support our families,” said Ahmed Rashwan, a housekeeping supervisor affected by the closures. “We ask for immediate solutions to protect hotel employees.”

Analysts warn the impact could deepen if the sanctions persist. “The hospitality sector in Egypt is a major employer with extensive local hiring,” noted economist Hossam Farouk. “If these restrictions continue, we may see widespread layoffs and a prolonged recovery.”

Officials at the Ministry of Tourism have stated they are in negotiations with international partners to resolve the dispute and restore normal operations at the affected sites. The situation remains fluid as talks continue.
